explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/453: is it true that for all large n there is i < n with p_n² < p_{n+i}p_{n−i}? Pomerance proved the answer is no. The statement negates the eventual existence claim using 0-indexed primes. The shift drops the single 1-indexed witness i = n−1 (the one involving p₁ = 2), which makes the negated statement marginally stronger. Pomerance's result, that infinitely often p_n² > p_{n+i}p_{n−i} for all 0 < i < n, implies it, so the formal statement holds exactly when the intended answer is no. Faithful.
